questions.stem: In triangle $ABC$, $a = 8\text{ cm}$, $b = 6\text{ cm}$, and $c = 10\text{ cm}$. Which expression finds angle $C$?
questions.explanation: To find angle $C$, rearrange the cosine rule: $\cos C = \frac{a^2 + b^2 - c^2}{2ab} = \frac{8^2 + 6^2 - 10^2}{2 \times 8 \times 6}$.

questions.stem: When should you use the cosine rule instead of the sine rule?

options.text: When you know two angles and one side
When you know all three angles
When you know two sides and the included angle, or all three sides

questions.explanation: The cosine rule is used when you know two sides and the included angle (SAS) to find the third side, or when you know all three sides (SSS) to find an angle.

questions.stem: In triangle $PQR$, $p = 5\text{ cm}$, $q = 5\text{ cm}$, and $r = 5\text{ cm}$. Using the cosine rule, what is angle $P$?
questions.explanation: $\cos P = \frac{q^2 + r^2 - p^2}{2qr} = \frac{25 + 25 - 25}{50} = \frac{25}{50} = 0.5$. So $P = \cos^{-1}(0.5) = 60°$. This confirms an equilateral triangle has all angles equal to $60°$.
